Justification: Defines acceptable use of IT systems and data for all employees.
Required for pre-employment screening; supports personnel security.
Board/management must oversee security strategy and risk.
Required to ensure availability of systems/data during interruptions.
Controls changes to systems to prevent unauthorized/unintended modifications.
Specific procedures for application/software changes; part of broader change control.
Emergency changes (hotfixes, critical patches) require expedited but documented approval.
Infrastructure changes (network, servers, storage) require change management.
Must separate request, approval, and implementation of changes.
All changes tracked in ticketing system (Jira) with approvals documented.
Establishes behavioral expectations and ethical standards for all personnel.
Privacy criteria; deferred to Phase 2 (SOC 2 Privacy audit).
Defines approved configurations for systems; prevents unauthorized/unintended settings.
Vendor/customer contracts must include security requirements and SLA commitments.
Classifies data by sensitivity; supports access control and protection decisions.
Visual representation of how data flows between systems; identifies protection points.
Defines data handling, storage, encryption, and transmission standards.
Specifies how long data is retained; ensures timely deletion when no longer needed.
Encrypts data at rest on all hard drives; prevents data exposure if device is lost/stolen.
Regular performance reviews support competency and behavioral expectations.
Controls access to shared drives; prevents unauthorized data access.
Encrypts data stored in databases, file systems, and backups.
Uses TLS/HTTPS for data in transit between systems; prevents eavesdropping.
Controls network traffic; restricts access to systems based on security policy.
All employees accountable for reporting security incidents; supports rapid response.
Documented procedures for detecting, investigating, and responding to incidents.
Regular drills/tabletop exercises test incident response capability; identifies gaps.
Procedures for reporting incidents to external parties (customers, regulators).
Monitors for and detects unauthorized access/intrusion attempts.
Defines roles, responsibilities, and required competencies for all positions.
Controls who can access systems/data; ties to identity/roles.
Monitors system health, performance, and security events; alerts on anomalies.
Current network architecture diagram; identifies critical systems and connections.
Vendor/contractor NDAs protect confidential information.
Current org structure; shows reporting lines and responsibility alignment.
Password policy specifying complexity, length, rotation, history requirements.
Procedures for creating/granting access when users/roles are added.
Documents action plans for identified risks; tracks remediation status.
Formal process for identifying, analyzing, and rating risks; supports decision-making.
Policy establishing frequency, scope, and governance of risk assessments.
Annual security awareness training for all personnel; builds security culture.
Developers cannot directly deploy to production; requires approval/separation.
IT operations cannot approve their own changes; independent reviewer required.
Development/test systems separate from production; prevents testing data in prod.
Complete description of systems in scope; describes components and data flow.
When employees leave, all access is removed timely (within 1 business day).
Require and review SOC 2 attestations from all critical vendors with data access.
Annual review of user access rights; removes unnecessary/outdated access.
Multi-factor authentication for critical systems; single sign-on where appropriate.
Evaluate vendor security posture before engagement; assess risk/capability.
Policy for managing vendor relationships; SLAs, monitoring, remediation.
Annual review of vendor performance, security posture, compliance status.
Register of vendor risks (concentration, SLA failure, security breach); mitigation plans.
Quarterly vulnerability scans on all systems; identifies and remediate security weaknesses.
Current hardware/software inventory; actively maintained (weekly updates).
Privileged admin accounts are logged, monitored, and reviewed regularly.
Antivirus deployed on all devices; updated daily; alerts monitored.
Patches applied automatically for OS and critical applications; tested before prod deployment.
